transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I guess what brings me in today is... well, it's my head. It just feels incredibly foggy lately, if that makes sense. 

I work as a personal care aide, you see, and I've been doing this for a long time, so I know the routines inside and out. It's usually completely second nature to me. But lately, I don't know, it's like my brain is walking through molasses. I'll be sitting there trying to write up my client notes at the end of the shift—which is super important, you know, because the next shift needs to know exactly what happened, if the client ate, if they were comfortable, all those details—and I'm just making these little mistakes. Just stupid, silly mistakes that I never make. 

And it's not just the paperwork, either. I'll be in the middle of helping a client, maybe heading to the kitchen to grab them a glass of water or going to the linen closet to fetch a fresh towel, and I'll just stop dead in the hallway. I completely forget what I was about to do. I just stand there trying to retrace my steps in my mind, trying to force my brain to work. 

It really isn't like me at all. I've always prided myself on being sharp and on top of things for my clients, because they rely on me so heavily, you know? I took some college classes a while back and I've always been good at keeping organized, but this whole... this whole fogginess is just really throwing me off my game and I just can't seem to shake it, no matter how hard I try to focus.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess... yeah, I have. It's funny you ask that, because I was just thinking about it the other morning. Lately, I'll wake up—and I'm usually an early riser, you know, getting up at 5:30 or 6:00 to get a jump on the day before my shift starts—but I'll wake up and before I even get out of bed, before my feet even hit the floor, there's just this... this heavy, completely empty feeling right here in my chest. It's like a physical weight, just sitting there. 

And I still get up, you know, I make my coffee, I pack my lunch, I put on my scrubs and I go to work. I can get through my shift, mostly, aside from that brain fog I was telling you about. I can still talk to my clients, ask them how their grandchildren are doing, smile and nod and do all the things a good aide is supposed to do. I mean, they need a friendly face, right? They don't need to see me looking miserable. But inside... inside, I just feel so sad. Just completely flat and sad, like the color has been drained out of everything. 

It's not like I'm sitting there crying in the breakroom or anything dramatic like that, but it's this constant, dull ache of sadness that just follows me around all day. Even when I come home and try to watch a baseball game or something I usually really like, I just sit there with that same empty feeling in my chest, just going through the motions of my day without really caring about any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual even after a full night's sleep?

Yeah, I have. I really have. And it's so frustrating because, like I said, I'm usually up early, ready to go. I'll get my seven or eight hours of sleep—I'm pretty strict about my sleep schedule, always have been, because in my line of work you really can't be running on fumes when people are depending on you. But lately, even after a full, solid night in bed, I wake up and my body just feels... well, it feels like I ran a marathon in my sleep. Just completely worn out. 

And it's not even like I'm doing heavy lifting all the time to justify it. Even on my days off, days where I literally don't do much of anything besides maybe puttering around the house or watching a bit of TV, I just feel this deep, heavy tiredness in my bones. 

And at work... man, work is getting tough. Just simple things, you know? Like, helping a client with a shower. Usually, that's just a standard part of the morning routine. You get the towels ready, you make sure the water temperature is right, you help them in, make sure they're safe, maybe help them wash their back... it's just a process I've done a thousand times. But lately, just doing that, just standing there and assisting them, it takes so much more out of me than it ever should. By the time they're dried off and dressed, I feel like I need to sit down in the armchair and catch my breath for ten minutes. 

Even just regular errands are doing it. I went to the grocery store the other day, just a quick trip to grab some milk, bread, a few apples, maybe some chicken for dinner. Nothing crazy, just two bags of groceries. And carrying those bags from my car to the front door... I had to stop and put them down on the porch step for a second. It's just ridiculous. I'm a 43-year-old man, I shouldn't be getting winded carrying a couple of grocery bags. But it just drains me. Everything just feels like it takes ten times the energy it used to, and I just don't understand why I can't just bounce back after a good night's rest like I normally do.
